Weekly planning routine: 8 ways to plan the week in under 30 minutes

A weekly planning routine is a short, repeated session, usually 15 to 30 minutes, where you clear last week, place the fixed commitments and choose a few outcomes for the week ahead.

Quick answer

Do it at the same time each week, fixed things first, then no more than three outcomes. Leave empty space every day; a full plan breaks on the first surprise.

Weekly Planning Routine in 20 Minutes: 6 Steps

  1. Clear last week's list
  2. Copy in fixed appointments
  3. Pick 3 outcomes for the week
  4. Give each one a day
  5. One focus block a day
  6. Leave Friday afternoon open

Sunday Reset Routine for the Week Ahead

  1. Laundry on, dishes done
  2. Look at the week's calendar
  3. Plan 3 easy dinners
  4. Pack Monday's bag
  5. Choose Monday's first task
  6. Bed 30 minutes early

Weekly Planner Method for Busy Weeks

  1. List every fixed commitment
  2. Mark the two busiest days
  3. Move what can wait
  4. One priority a day
  5. Errands in one trip
  6. The week on one page

Weekly Reset Checklist You Can Finish in 15 Minutes

  1. Empty your bag and desk
  2. Inbox down to 10
  3. Pay or schedule bills
  4. Delete finished tasks
  5. Check next week's deadlines
  6. Set Monday's first task

Weekly Planning for Founders: A 6-Step Monday Routine

  1. Review last week's numbers
  2. Pick the one number that matters
  3. Three outcomes, no more
  4. Two deep-work mornings
  5. Meetings on two days
  6. Book the Friday review

Weekly Planning Review: 6 Questions in 10 Minutes

  1. What got done?
  2. What slipped, and why?
  3. What did I promise people?
  4. What can I drop?
  5. Next week's 3 outcomes?
  6. When is my first focus block?

Weekly Planner Routine Without Overplanning

  1. One page, not a spread
  2. Three outcomes only
  3. Fixed things first
  4. Empty space every day
  5. Only a top task each day
  6. Stop after 20 minutes

Weekly Planning on Monday Morning in 15 Minutes

  1. Calendar before the inbox
  2. Note what changed since Friday
  3. Pick this week's 3 outcomes
  4. Book them into real slots
  5. Tell people what you'll deliver
  6. Start outcome one

Frequently asked questions

When is the best time to plan the week?

Whenever you can protect it every week: Sunday evening, Monday morning or Friday afternoon all work. The habit matters more than the day.

How many goals should a week have?

Three outcomes is a good ceiling. More than that and the week turns into a wish list.

Do I need a paper planner?

No. One page, a notes app or a calendar is enough. What matters is that the plan fits on one screen or one sheet.
